note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording and the translator-rendered Old Testament verses the first edition carried.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse or range, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. The sermon text (Ezek 33:11) heads each sermon as the whole OWB verse, and Baxter's refrain 'Turn ye, turn ye, why will ye die?' is OWB's own words joined with '…' («ተመለሱ፤ ከክፉ መንገዳችሁ ተመለሱ! … ለምን ትሞታላችሁ?»), identical everywhere it recurs. OWB's inner quotation marks become ‹› inside the book's «». John 3:3 reads 'born from above' in OWB; the first quotation in each sermon that argues from the new birth carries the gloss (ማለትም ዳግመኛ ካልተወለደ). Where Baxter interleaves his own gloss in a verse (Mark 16:16 'that is with such a converting faith', Luke 24:47 'which is conversion'), the gloss stands in parentheses between OWB pieces. 'Strive to enter in at the strait gate' is Baxter's join of Luke 13:24 and Matt 7:13-14; each piece is quoted from its own verse. Where the quoted words stand in another verse the citation follows them (1 Cor 3:19 for 'the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God'; Acts 26:14 for 'kick against the pricks').

`self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are Baxter's allusions, paraphrases, conflations and re-personed recitations (God's pleas in his own words, 'your damnation slumbereth not', 'they will not come to me'), and Ps 145:17, where Baxter argues from 'holy' and OWB reads 'faithful'.
